summary: The audit checks COMPLIT 346, DLCL 301, DLCL 369 and the COMPLIT 397 colloquium, letter graded where a letter grade is offered, and 135 units in all, counting only graduate-level listings. You check by hand the six primary-field and four complementary courses, the First-Year Colloquium and Qualifying Paper, certification in three languages (your native language, an advanced second and an intermediate third) by spring of your second year, candidacy, the University Oral Exam, the Prospectus Colloquium and the dissertation. A grade of B or below is reviewed by the faculty but does not by itself stop a course from counting.

ywZBwlZf-text.why: "Students must demonstrate competence in three languages in total ... Proficiency in languages will be formally assessed during graduate study and must be certified before admission to candidacy by examination administered through the Stanford Language Center." The same requirement as rule ov-languages under Advancement to Candidacy, which now carries the levels and the spring of year two deadline. Designating two primary literatures "by completing six or more graduate courses in that literature" is a choice, not a requirement.

TnUo2KFw.why: "Enrollment in COMPLIT 397 (Graduate Studies Colloquium) is required each quarter that the student is in the program". The quarter-by-quarter enrollment is not counted; one enrollment satisfies the rule. Grading: "Ph.D. students in the department must take required courses for a letter grade if available".
